questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: Which of these is an example of an IoT system?

options.text: A table fan that is switched on with its regulator
A battery torch that glows when its button is pressed
A smart water meter in a Pune housing society that sends daily water use to the residents' mobile app
A pressure cooker that whistles when the steam builds up

questions.chapter: 1. Understanding IoT – 1.2 What is IoT?
questions.explanation: The water meter senses data, sends it over the internet and shows it in an app. The other devices work alone and share no data.

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: Ananya's mixer-grinder is electric and has a powerful motor. Why is it still NOT an IoT device?

options.text: It works only when someone operates it and does not share data with other devices or the internet.
It uses electricity instead of batteries.
It has a motor, and IoT devices never have motors.
It is used in the kitchen, and IoT is used only in offices.

questions.chapter: 1. Understanding IoT – 1.4 This is Not IoT
questions.explanation: A non-IoT device works alone and needs a human to operate it every time; IoT devices connect, share data and decide on their own.

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: Seventy-year-old Harbhajan Ji in Ludhiana wears a smart patch after heart treatment. Which order correctly shows how his health data reaches his doctor?

options.text: Cloud → home hub → patch sensors → doctor → Bluetooth
Home hub → doctor → patch sensors → cloud → Bluetooth
Doctor → cloud → Bluetooth → patch sensors → home hub
Patch sensors → Bluetooth → home hub → cloud → alert to the doctor

questions.chapter: 1. Understanding IoT – 1.3 IoT Stories
questions.explanation: The patch first senses the readings, sends them by Bluetooth to a home hub, which forwards them to the cloud; the system then alerts the doctor.

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: Which part of an IoT system works like its "eyes and ears", collecting raw data from the surroundings?
questions.chapter: 2. Main Components of an IoT System – 2.1 Sensors
questions.explanation: Sensors gather information such as temperature, light, sound and movement from the environment.

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: Kavya's wireless earbuds connect to her phone without any cable. Which connectivity technology are they most likely using?
questions.chapter: 2. Main Components of an IoT System – 2.2 Connectivity
questions.explanation: Bluetooth / BLE is used for short-range, energy-efficient communication, such as wireless earbuds.

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: A farmer in Rajasthan places battery-powered soil sensors in fields several kilometres from his house. The sensors send only a little data each day. Which connectivity option suits this best?
questions.chapter: 2. Main Components of an IoT System – 2.2 Connectivity
questions.explanation: LoRaWAN is designed for long-range, low-power communication, which suits remote, battery-powered farm sensors.

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: What does "edge computing" mean in an IoT system?

options.text: Processing data on or near the device itself so that decisions are faster
Showing data on a web dashboard
Sending sensor readings to users by SMS
Storing all data only on distant cloud servers

questions.chapter: 2. Main Components of an IoT System – 2.3 Data Processing
questions.explanation: In edge computing, processing happens right on the device (at the "edge"), giving faster decisions.

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: In a smart drip-irrigation system on a sugarcane farm in Maharashtra, which component is the actuator?

options.text: The mobile app that shows moisture levels
The valve that opens to let water flow to the plants
The Wi-Fi router that sends data to the cloud
The soil moisture sensor buried near the roots

questions.chapter: 2. Main Components of an IoT System – 2.4 Actuators
questions.explanation: Actuators perform physical actions. The valve controls the flow of water; the sensor senses, the app displays and the router connects.

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly shows how the components of an IoT system work together?
questions.chapter: 2. Main Components of an IoT System – 2.6 How Components Work Together
questions.explanation: Sensors sense, connectivity carries the data, processing makes decisions, actuators act and the system learns from patterns.

questions.prompt: How is a microcontroller different from a laptop computer?

options.text: A microcontroller runs a full operating system and many programs at once.
A microcontroller can only be used for web browsing and gaming.
A microcontroller is always bigger and more powerful than a laptop.
A microcontroller is a tiny computer on a single chip that controls one specific task.

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.1 Microcontroller vs Computer
questions.explanation: A microcontroller is a "brain on a chip" for one job, used in devices such as washing machines; a laptop is a general-purpose, multitasking computer.

questions.prompt: A street light in Bhopal switches on automatically when it gets dark. Which part is the "Think" step of the Sense–Think–Act loop?

options.text: The program deciding, "If it is dark, turn on the light"
The lamp glowing on the street
The relay switching on the lamp
The light sensor measuring how bright it is

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.2 Sense–Think–Act Loop
questions.explanation: In the "Think" step, the controller runs its program to decide what to do; sensing and acting are the steps before and after.

questions.prompt: The crystal oscillator on an Arduino Uno is marked "16.000". What does this tell us?

options.text: The board needs a 16-volt power supply.
It runs at 16 MHz and helps the board keep track of time.

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.4 Arduino Uno Board
questions.explanation: The crystal oscillator sets the timing; 16.000 means a frequency of 16,000,000 Hz, that is 16 MHz.

questions.prompt: Kavya wants to make an LED glow dimly and brightly on her Arduino Uno using analogWrite(). Which kind of pin should she connect the LED to?

options.text: A digital pin marked with "~", such as pin 9

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.4 Arduino Uno Board
questions.explanation: Six of the 14 digital pins can give PWM output; they are marked "~" and are used with analogWrite() for dimming.

questions.prompt: Students in Jaipur want to stitch LEDs and a small controller into a jacket for a science fair. Which Arduino board is designed for clothing and textile projects?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.5 Popular Arduino Boards
questions.explanation: The LilyPad is made for smart clothing and textile projects; the Mega suits projects needing many connections.

questions.prompt: Which of these sensors gives an analog output (a range of values) rather than only 0 or 1?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.6.1 Digital and Analog Sensors
questions.explanation: An LDR's value changes continuously with light (for example 0 to 1023 on Arduino). PIR, IR and touch sensors give digital 0/1 outputs.

questions.prompt: How does the HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor measure distance?

options.text: By sensing the heat given off by a body
By detecting a change in capacitance
By measuring how bright the light is
By sending sound waves and timing their echo

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.6.1 Sensors
questions.explanation: The ultrasonic sensor uses sound waves; the time taken for the echo to return gives the distance.

questions.prompt: The school canteen in Indore wants a touchless sanitiser dispenser that works only when a hand is held just below the nozzle, not when people walk across the room. Which sensor is the best choice?

options.text: PIR sensor, which detects motion anywhere in its wide field of view
IR sensor, which detects an object close to it by infrared reflection
LDR, which senses the brightness of the room
DHT11, which measures temperature and humidity

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.6.1 Sensors
questions.explanation: An IR sensor detects nearby objects (proximity). A PIR sensor would react to people moving across the room.

questions.prompt: A 3D printer in a Bengaluru makerspace must move its print head in small, exact steps. Which motor is best for this?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.6.2 Actuators (Motors)
questions.explanation: Stepper motors rotate in precise steps, which is why they are used in 3D printers and CNC machines.

questions.prompt: Which component lets students build and test a circuit without soldering?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.6.4 Other Components
questions.explanation: A breadboard is used to build and test circuits without soldering.

questions.prompt: What is an Arduino program called, and what is its file extension?

options.text: A script, saved with the extension .py
A sheet, saved with the extension .xls
An app, saved with the extension .apk
A sketch, saved with the extension .ino

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.8 Basics of Arduino Programming
questions.explanation: In Arduino, a program is called a sketch and is saved as an .ino file.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the two main functions of an Arduino sketch is correct?

options.text: loop() runs once first, and then setup() repeats forever.
setup() runs once when the board starts; loop() then runs again and again.
setup() runs every second, and loop() runs only when a button is pressed.
Both setup() and loop() run only once.

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.8 Basics of Arduino Programming
questions.explanation: setup() is used for one-time settings such as pinMode; loop() holds the main logic and repeats until the power is switched off.

questions.prompt: Rohan's code is: int value = analogRead(A0); if (value > 600) { digitalWrite(8, HIGH); } else { digitalWrite(8, LOW); }. If the sensor on A0 gives the value 450, what happens to the LED on pin 8?

options.text: It stays OFF, because 450 is not greater than 600.
The board resets because the value is too low.
It turns ON, because 450 is a valid analog value.

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.8 Basics of Arduino Programming
questions.explanation: The condition value > 600 is false for 450, so the else part runs and pin 8 is set LOW.

questions.prompt: In the Blink program, both delay(1000) lines are changed to delay(250). What will happen?

options.text: The LED will blink slower: ON for 250 seconds.
The LED will stay ON all the time.
The LED will blink faster: ON for 0.25 second and OFF for 0.25 second.

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.9 Blink Program
questions.explanation: delay() counts in milliseconds; 250 ms is a quarter of a second, so the blinking becomes faster.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Tinkercad is correct?

options.text: It can be programmed only with text code, not with blocks.
It is used only for 3D design and cannot simulate circuits.
It must be installed on the computer and works only when a real Arduino is connected.
It is a free, browser-based tool from Autodesk for building and testing virtual Arduino circuits before making them for real.

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.10 Tinkercad Simulation
questions.explanation: Tinkercad runs in a web browser, simulates circuits with Arduino, and supports both block and text coding, as well as 3D design.

questions.prompt: In the motion-sensor project, Meera connects the PIR sensor's OUT pin to digital pin 2. Her code begins with int pirPin = 3; and the LED never turns on, even when she simulates motion. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The PIR sensor should be connected to the AREF pin.
The LED needs a 9-volt battery to glow.
The code reads pin 3, but the sensor is wired to pin 2.
Serial.begin(9600) stops the LED from working.

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.10 Project: Motion Sensor with LED
questions.explanation: The program reads the wrong pin, so it never sees the HIGH signal from the PIR sensor; pirPin should be 2.

questions.prompt: Your phone's screen becomes brighter outdoors and dimmer indoors on its own. Which sensor makes this happen?

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: Meera's smartwatch keeps sending her location to her parents even when her phone is at home. Which connectivity does it use?

Comparing historical data to predict next year's crop
An automatic trigger based on a preset threshold

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)

questions.section: Section A – IoT Basics and Components   (Questions 1–9)
questions.prompt: Which of these is the user interface of a smart water-tank system?

options.text: The Wi-Fi router in the house
A mobile app that shows the tank's water level
The water-level sensor inside the tank
The pump motor on the roof

questions.chapter: 2. Main Components of an IoT System – 2.5 User Interface
questions.explanation: The user interface is the part people interact with, such as apps, dashboards and alerts.

questions.prompt: Which of these appliances most likely has a microcontroller doing one fixed job?

options.text: A laptop used for browsing and gaming
A desktop computer running office software
A tablet used for video calls

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.1 What is a Microcontroller?
questions.explanation: The book gives washing machines and microwaves as examples of embedded systems with microcontrollers.

questions.prompt: Which microcontroller does the book describe as having built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth for connecting projects to the internet?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.2 Microcontrollers in IoT
questions.explanation: The book describes the ESP32/ESP8266 as powerful chips with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

questions.prompt: What is the simplest way to power an Arduino Uno while programming it from a computer?

options.text: Through the USB cable connected to the computer
Through the TX and RX pins

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.4 Arduino Uno Board
questions.explanation: The Uno can be powered by the USB cable connected to the computer.

questions.prompt: What do the TX and RX LEDs on an Arduino Uno show?

options.text: They show that the board is powered on.
They show the value read on an analog pin.
They flash when the board is sending and receiving serial data.
They glow when the reset button is pressed.

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.4 Arduino Uno Board
questions.explanation: TX (transmit) flashes while sending and RX (receive) while receiving serial data.

questions.prompt: Aarav wants to build a custom gaming controller that a computer recognises like a keyboard. Which board does the book suggest for such tasks?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.5 Popular Arduino Boards
questions.explanation: The Leonardo is used for automation and computer-control tasks, such as gaming controllers and custom keyboards.

questions.prompt: Which sensor would you use to detect leaking cooking gas in a kitchen?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.6.1 Sensors
questions.explanation: MQ-series gas sensors detect gases and are used for gas-leak detection.

questions.prompt: How does a soil moisture sensor measure the water content of the soil?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.6.1 Sensors
questions.explanation: Wet soil conducts electricity better, so the sensor measures water content using conductivity.

questions.prompt: Which pair is classified correctly, as in the book?

options.text: Touch sensor – analog; temperature sensor – digital
PIR sensor – analog; gas sensor – digital
IR sensor – analog; PIR sensor – analog

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.6.1 Digital and Analog Sensors
questions.explanation: The book lists IR, PIR and touch sensors as digital, and LDR, gas and temperature sensors as analog.

questions.prompt: A robotic arm in a school lab must turn its gripper to exactly 90 degrees. Which motor is best?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.6.2 Actuators (Motors)
questions.explanation: A servo motor rotates to a controlled, fixed angle, which is why it is used in robotic arms.

questions.prompt: A school kabaddi scoreboard needs to show only numbers from 0 to 9 in each digit. Which output device is most suitable?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.6.3 Output Devices
questions.explanation: A 7-segment display shows numbers and is used in counters and scoreboards.

questions.prompt: In Arduino code, how must every command end?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.8 Basics of Arduino Programming
questions.explanation: Every Arduino command ends with a semicolon, like a full stop at the end of a sentence.

questions.prompt: Which variable type should store a body temperature reading of 36.6?
questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.8 Variables
questions.explanation: "float" stores numbers with decimals; "int" stores only whole numbers.

questions.prompt: What does this code do? for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) { digitalWrite(13, HIGH); delay(200); digitalWrite(13, LOW); delay(200); }

options.text: Blinks the LED 3 times, taking 1.2 seconds in total
Blinks the LED 4 times, taking 1.6 seconds in total
Blinks the LED 4 times, taking 0.8 second in total
Blinks the LED 5 times, taking 2 seconds in total

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.8 Loops
questions.explanation: i takes the values 0, 1, 2 and 3, so the LED blinks 4 times; each blink takes 200 + 200 = 400 ms, so 4 × 400 ms = 1.6 s.

questions.prompt: In the Blink program, what does digitalWrite(13, HIGH) do?

options.text: It reads whether pin 13 is HIGH or LOW.
It sends 0 V to pin 13 and turns the LED off.
It makes pin 13 an input pin.
It sends 5 V to pin 13 and turns the LED on.

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.9 Blink Program
questions.explanation: HIGH means "send 5 V", which turns the LED on; LOW sends 0 V.

questions.prompt: In the motion-sensor project, why is a 220 Ω resistor connected with the LED?

options.text: To make the LED blink automatically
To limit the current so that the LED is not damaged
To help the PIR sensor detect motion
To store the program on the board

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.10 Project: Motion Sensor with LED
questions.explanation: A resistor controls the current flowing in the circuit and protects the LED.

questions.prompt: In the motion-sensor project, Kavya wants the LED to stay ON for 5 seconds each time motion is detected. What is the best change?

options.text: Change int ledPin = 13; to int ledPin = 2;
Change pinMode(pirPin, INPUT) to pinMode(pirPin, OUTPUT)
Add delay(5000); after digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); inside the if block

questions.chapter: 3. IoT with Arduino – 3.10 Project: Motion Sensor with LED
questions.explanation: A 5000 ms delay after switching the LED on keeps it on for 5 seconds before the loop checks again.
